source_claims.quote: Another object commonly seen in Saraswati's hands is the vina (the Hindu classical music instrument) which reminds of her gift of music to humanity.

statement.id: Vina sering digambarkan berada di tangan Saraswati.
statement.en: Saraswati is often depicted holding a vina.

source_claims.quote: Her attributes—the vina (a symbol of music and the arts), palm-sized manuscript (a symbol of learning), and rosary (a symbol of religious rites)—denote her role as a goddess of knowledge.

statement.id: Vina, manuskrip, dan tasbih menjadi atributnya yang melambangkan musik, pembelajaran, dan ritus.
statement.en: Her vina, manuscript, and rosary symbolize music, learning, and ritual.

source_claims.quote: Saraswati is conventionally accompanied by a swan, but a peacock stands beside her here, enchanted by the divine music she creates.

statement.id: Saraswati secara konvensional ditemani angsa, sementara satu cetakan menampilkan merak.
statement.en: Saraswati is conventionally accompanied by a swan, though this print shows a peacock.

source_claims.quote: Originally associated with an ancient lost river that bore her name, Saraswati increasingly came to be celebrated as the goddess of all waters and their life-giving and purifying powers.

statement.id: Saraswati awalnya terkait sungai kuno senama, lalu dipuja sebagai dewi seluruh perairan.
statement.en: Saraswati was associated with a lost river of the same name and later with all waters.

source_claims.quote: The Saraswati River (modern name: Sarsuti), just like the Ganges River, flows from the Himalaya and is considered a sacred source of purification, fertility, and good fortune for those who bathe in her waters. The sacred river, again like the Ganges, then developed into a personified deity.

statement.id: Sungai Saraswati (nama modern: Sarsuti), seperti Sungai Gangga, mengalir dari Himalaya dan dianggap sumber suci penyucian, kesuburan, dan keberuntungan bagi mereka yang mandi di airnya; sungai suci itu kemudian berkembang menjadi dewi yang dipersonifikasikan.
statement.en: The Saraswati River (modern name Sarsuti), like the Ganges, flows from the Himalaya and is considered a sacred source of purification, fertility, and good fortune for those who bathe in it; the sacred river then developed into a personified deity.

source_claims.quote: In Hindu art, Saraswati is usually depicted as a graceful youth with white skin. She most often wears a white sari (which symbolises purity) which has a blue border.

statement.id: Dalam seni Hindu, Saraswati biasanya digambarkan sebagai remaja anggun berkulit putih, paling sering berkain sari putih (lambang kesucian) bertepi biru.
statement.en: In Hindu art Saraswati is usually shown as a graceful youth with white skin, most often in a white sari (symbolizing purity) with a blue border.

source_claims.quote: As with many Hindu deities, Saraswati is often depicted with four arms, each holding a symbolic object. In the left hands she can carry a palm-leaf manuscript and ritual water vessel. In the upper right hand she holds a white lotus flower

statement.id: Seperti banyak dewa Hindu, Saraswati sering digambarkan berlengan empat, masing-masing memegang benda lambang; di tangan kiri ia dapat membawa manuskrip daun lontar dan bejana air ritual, dan di tangan kanan atas ia memegang teratai putih.
statement.en: Like many Hindu deities, Saraswati is often shown with four arms, each holding a symbolic object; in the left hands she can carry a palm-leaf manuscript and a ritual water vessel, and in the upper right hand she holds a white lotus.

source_claims.quote: She with her might, like one who digs for lotus-stems, hath burst with her strong waves the ridges of the hills.

statement.id: Dalam himne Rigveda (terjemahan Griffith), Sarasvati dengan kekuatannya menjebol punggung bukit dengan ombaknya yang deras, seperti orang yang menggali batang teratai.
statement.en: In a Rigveda hymn (Griffith's translation), Sarasvati with her might bursts the ridges of the hills with her strong waves, like one who digs for lotus stems.
